questions.stem: Why does an orbiting spacecraft remain affected by the gravity of Earth?
options: Earth gravity has the same strength at every altitude.
Gravity continues to act at orbital altitude.
Free fall eliminates the gravitational force.
Orbital motion requires continuous engine thrust.
questions.explanation: The gravity of Earth remains significant in orbit and continuously bends the spacecraft trajectory.

questions.stem: In an ideal unpowered gravity assist, what can change relative to the Sun?
options: The gravitational parameter of the flyby body
The spacecraft mass by burning propellant
The speed of light in vacuum
The spacecraft trajectory and velocity
questions.explanation: A flyby exchanges a small amount of orbital energy and momentum with the encountered body, changing the heliocentric motion of the spacecraft.

questions.stem: Why must a pressurised spacecraft structure withstand stress?
options: The cabin pressure is exactly balanced by the vacuum.
A pressure difference loads solar panels only.
Interior pressure differs from the surrounding vacuum.
Pressure loads disappear whenever the spacecraft orbits.
questions.explanation: The difference between internal and external pressure loads the cabin structure.

questions.stem: Why may a spacecraft change temperature between sunlight and shadow?
options: Earth gravity varies between sunlight and shadow.
The spacecraft must use propulsion in sunlight.
Its exposure to incoming solar radiation changes.
Vacuum maintains the same temperature on all surfaces.
questions.explanation: Sunlight, reflected radiation and its own heat balance vary with its environment and orientation.

questions.stem: How does an exposed radiator mainly reject heat to space?
options: By ordinary external air convection
By radiation from its surface
By conduction directly into the vacuum
By carrying heat away in the surrounding air
questions.explanation: In near vacuum, a radiator rejects heat mainly by thermal radiation.

questions.stem: What can a spacecraft thermal-control fluid loop do?
options: Generate electrical power from sunlight
Measure the spacecraft attitude
Store the communications signal
Transfer heat between components
questions.explanation: A fluid loop transports thermal energy within a spacecraft, often toward a radiator.

questions.stem: What is the main energy-conversion function of spacecraft solar panels?
options: Thermal energy only, without electricity
Electrical energy regardless of illumination
Electrical energy from sunlight
Mechanical thrust directly from reflected sunlight
questions.explanation: Solar cells convert part of incident sunlight into electricity; output depends on illumination and other conditions.

questions.stem: Which task belongs to a crew life-support system?
options: Point the communications antenna
Maintain breathable air and remove carbon dioxide
Control the spacecraft orbit
Regulate solar-panel orientation
questions.explanation: Life support manages the cabin environment, including oxygen supply and carbon-dioxide removal.

questions.stem: Why is propellant planning important for a spacecraft?
options: Onboard propellant is a finite resource.
The same propellant mass is available after every burn.
Solar panels consume propellant to generate electricity.
Guidance makes propellant unnecessary for a burn.
questions.explanation: Most spacecraft carry a limited propellant supply, so manoeuvres must be budgeted.

questions.stem: Why is the radiation environment considered in spacecraft design?
options: Only visible light affects spacecraft systems.
Orbital radiation affects people but not electronics.
Radiation protection replaces thermal control.
Energetic radiation can affect people and electronics.
questions.explanation: Energetic particles and other radiation can damage electronics and create health risks, so protection and mission planning matter.
